title: gateway oscore recipient store: deleting BOTH state and floor files resets the replay window (dual-FS compromise residual)
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), security pass. gateway.rs:447-458: (None,None) is interpreted as 'never seen' and returns empty, so an attacker who deletes both recipient-<hex> (state FS) and recipient-<hex>-floor (floor FS) for a previously-initialized context resets the replay window; subsequent genuine captured ciphertexts are accepted in ascending PIV order (capture-history replay incl. re-executable GCP commands). Every PARTIAL attack fails closed (delete state only -> Corrupt; stale state vs floor -> Corrupt; swaps/forges/truncates -> Corrupt; heal cannot elevate trust). Production requires the floor root on a different filesystem (verify_independent_rollback_root dev() check, lichend.rs:1408-1425), so full reset needs compromise of two independent rollback domains - the inherent limit of software-only anti-rollback (no monotonic counter), RFC 8613 s7.5-class residual. Action: document the residual explicitly in the threat-model section of the gateway docs; consider optionally recording a 'context ever-initialized' tombstone on the floor FS so single-FS deletion plus independent-FS state deletion cannot recreate the (None,None) fresh appearance.
